interpretations.answer: The total average effect of receiving t=1 rather than t=0 on y is estimated to be 5.137751952370555 (95% CI: 4.934846069047842, 5.3601749844607784) by the propensity score weighting design, and 4.912123614802114 (95% CI: 4.796817045052623, 5.031936958434754) by the general linear model design. Both designs assume unconfoundedness, consistency, and no interference, with graph relationships explicitly assumed and omitted identification-relevant edges treated as conditional graph assumptions.
caveats: The causal relationship between t and y (rel:edge.t.y) is contested and cannot be confirmed before the design freeze.

The propensity score weighting design shows sensitivity to unobserved confounding, with the effect ranging from -1.2859603531902886 to 4.843333286454968 under simulated confounders (sensitivity:de442b417c17c.1_vs_0.add_unobserved_common_cause.range).
Balance for covariate c was a soft pass for both designs, with a standardized mean difference of 1.322 before adjustment (check:de442b417c17c.1_vs_0.balance.c, check:dd2fd6efa4009.1_vs_0.balance.c).

Summarize diagnostic implications instead of reproducing every diagnostic number. Cite displayed addresses, and reproduce every number accurately. Do not state uncited ordinal counts or diagnostic thresholds. Distinguish graph-implied zero from measured effects. Discuss each surviving design and identify which relationship assumptions split them. Compare estimates only within the displayed numerical comparison groups, which require identical full target definitions and frozen analysis rows as well as contrast and scale. Name compared design IDs explicitly; describe incompatible target or support differences as caveats. A pass check records that its stated condition was met; never describe a passed requirement as missing. Frozen model declarations name the actual estimator, model covariates and provided baseline modifiers. An arm-separation AUC near one half means the covariates do not distinguish treatment arms well, which supports overlap rather than invalidating it. Passing falsification tests cannot establish causal validity or justify changing the pre-frozen lead design. LATE, natural effects and subgroup effects cannot be claimed to agree with total ATE merely because values are close. Include failed computations, unresolved assumptions, sensitivity ranges, and falsification caveats. Sensitivity has no pass verdict. Give descriptive comparisons, not a universal agreement score.
